Yes. For a bridal alteration business in Markham, I’d prioritize agencies that can generate actual fitting enquiries/bookings, rather than agencies focused mainly on followers or generic branding.

Agencies I’d shortlist

MRCK marketing — Markham. Strong performance-marketing orientation, including Google Ads, paid social, SEO, remarketing and analytics. They specifically describe online lead generation as one of their services and have been operating from Markham since 2015. 
mrckmarketing.com

Best for: Google Ads + measurable lead generation.

SearchSpark- Digital Marketing Agency — Markham. Offers SEO, local SEO, PPC and website work, with an emphasis on measurable lead growth.
Best for: Building a combination of Google search visibility and paid leads.

Elevate Talent & Marketing — Markham. Offers Google Ads/PPC and social media marketing, including Instagram/Facebook.
Best for: A visually driven bridal business where Instagram/Meta advertising can complement Google.

Click Media Lab — Markham. Full-service digital marketing with local SEO, SEO content and paid marketing capabilities.
Best for: Improving your Google presence while also working on the website.

True-E Digital Marketing — Markham. Focuses on websites, SEO, paid advertising and social media for small/midsized businesses.
Best for: A smaller-business-oriented marketing partner.

SearchKings — nearby in Scarborough, but worth considering because of its substantial Google Ads/local-search operation and very large review base.
Best for: A more specialized, lead-generation-heavy Google strategy.

There are also several other agencies specifically advertising Markham SEO/PPC services, including Preeminent Marketing, Eyeshot and SOAP Media.

What I'd actually do for your business

For bridal alterations, I'd not start with broad "social media management." I'd want an agency to build a system around searches such as:

"bridal alterations Markham"

"wedding dress alterations Markham"

"bridal seamstress near me"

"wedding dress fitting Markham"

"bridal alterations Richmond Hill"

"wedding dress alterations Vaughan"

Then send those people to a dedicated fitting page with strong photos, testimonials, your service area, starting-price guidance if appropriate, and a very obvious "Book a Fitting" / "Request an Appointment" button.

I'd combine Google Search Ads + Google Business Profile/local SEO initially. Instagram/Facebook retargeting can then remind people who visited your site but didn't book.

The important thing is to make the agency agree to measure qualified fitting enquiries, not clicks, impressions or followers. A good setup should tell you something like:

$X spent → Y enquiries → Z fittings booked → $ revenue

rather than simply "your traffic increased 40%."

If you tell me roughly what you charge for a typical bridal alteration and how much you'd be comfortable spending per month on marketing (e.g. $1k, $2k, $3k+), I can narrow this down to 3 agencies I'd contact first and what I'd ask each one to do.
